title: Intensive Language-Action Therapy combined with Acceptance and Commitment Therapy for group-based transdisciplinary treatment of post-stroke depression and aphasia (SYNERGY)
summary: About one-third of all stroke survivors suffer a profound loss of language function, known as aphasia. This loss increases the risk of developing mood disorders. Indeed, diagnosis of aphasia has proved to be a key predictor of post-stroke depression. However, current forms of treatment focus primarily on restoring language function, whereas the psychosocial consequences of aphasia have received less attention. The present randomized controlled trial seeks to determine whether or not combined treatment with methods borrowed from speech-language pathology and psychotherapy may potentially benefit verbal expression and alleviate post-stroke depression. The protocol includes Intensive Language-Action Therapy (ILAT), a group-based neurorehabilitative approach that uses communicative-pragmatic resources to promote progress in language performance, as demonstrated by a large number of randomized controlled trials. Moreover, preliminary evidence suggests that ILAT may also reduce symptoms of post-stroke depression. To address the psychological dimension of aphasia, ILAT is augmented with Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT), a treatment approach established in clinical psychology that encourages clients to adapt to irreversible loss while using remaining agency after stroke.

interventions.name: Intervention group (immediate start): ILAT combined with ACT; 3-week intensive intervention phase; frequency: 3 sessions per week, each lasting 2.5 hours per day (2 hours of ILAT, 0.5 hours of ACT); total treatment dosage: 22.5 hours

Waiting-list control group (delayed start): ILAT combined with ACT; 3-week waiting period, followed by 3-week intensive intervention phase; frequency: 3 sessions per week, each lasting 2.5 hours per day (2 hours of ILAT, 0.5 hours of ACT); total treatment dosage: 22.5 hours
